question: What current good manufacturing practice requirements apply to the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of animal food?
selected_labels: FDA Guidance: Draft Guidance for Industry: Questions and Answers on the Accredited Third-Party Certification Program (draft, 2022-04-28, Docket FDA-2022-D-0370)
FDA Guidance: CVM GFI #235 Current Good Manufacturing Practice Requirements for Food for Animals (final, 2017-10-20, Docket FDA-2016-D-1229)

answer:
The current good manufacturing practice requirements apply to the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of animal food as outlined in the FDA guidance. These requirements include:

- Preventive Controls for Animal Food (PCAF) which apply to the manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding of animal food. The scope generally applies to facilities required to register with the FDA under section 415 of the FD&C Act because they manufacture, process, pack, or hold animal food for consumption in the United States (21 CFR 507.5(a)), unless an exemption applies. [1]

- Preventive Controls for Human Food (PCHF) which apply to the manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding of human food. [2]

The guidance also specifies that for facilities manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding animal food, the CGMP regulations in 21 CFR part 507, subpart B, and the hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls regulations in 21 CFR part 507, subpart C apply. [1]

question: What supply-chain program requirements apply to an animal food facility, and when is the receiving facility responsible for it?

answer: The supply-chain program requirements apply to an animal food facility, and the receiving facility is responsible for it. The receiving facility must ensure that raw materials and other ingredients for their products are received only from approved suppliers, or if received on a temporary basis from unapproved suppliers, they must be subject to verification activities. The requirements include establishing and implementing a supply-chain program, determining appropriate supplier verification activities, and conducting supplier verification activities for raw materials and other ingredients. The program must be implemented in accordance with 21 CFR 507.110 and 507.115. If a facility has identified a hazard requiring a preventive control and relies on a control applied in the supply chain before receipt, it must have a supply-chain program. The program is not required for facilities that control all identified hazards with their own preventive controls or that rely solely on a commercial customer to control hazards. The program applies to all animal food facilities subject to the supply-chain program requirements of this rule. [1][2][3].

question: What requirements apply to medicated feed manufacturing and to veterinary feed directive drugs?
selected_labels: FDA Guidance: CVM GFI #120 Veterinary Feed Directive Regulation Questions and Answers (final, 2024-04-29, Docket FDA-2010-N-0155)
FDA Guidance: CVM GFI #120 Veterinary Feed Directive Regulation Questions and Answers (final, 2024-04-29, Docket FDA-2010-N-0155)

answer: The requirements for medicated feed manufacturing include a medicated feed mill license if the VFD drug used to manufacture a Type B or Type C medicated feed is a Category II, Type A medicated article (21 CFR 558.4(a)). A list of Category II drugs is provided in 21 CFR 558.4(d). A license is not required if the VFD drug used to manufacture a Type B or Type C medicated feed is a Category I, Type A medicated article, with the exception of certain liquid and free-choice medicated feeds. If you are a university researcher and want to perform research on a drug in medicated feed, you do not need a VFD to obtain the medicated feed. The VFD regulations apply to the use of VFD drugs and VFD feed for approved, conditionally approved, and indexed indications. When investigating a new indication during the approval process or performing tests in vitro or in animals used only for laboratory research purposes, the VFD regulations do not apply. Instead, the requirements in 21 CFR part 511 “New Animal Drugs for Investigational Use” apply. If you are shipping/distributing the VFD feed directly to the client, an acknowledgment letter alone from the dealer would not be sufficient. Instead, the dealer would also need to provide you with a copy of the VFD, and both you and your dealer are required to maintain a copy of the VFD for 2 years. The dealer must ensure that any medicated feed you distribute containing a VFD drug or combination VFD drug complies with the terms of the VFD and is manufactured and labeled in conformity with the approved, conditionally approved, or indexed conditions of use for such drug. [1]

question: What is required for a biologics license application under Part 601?
answer: Under Part 601, a biologics license application must be submitted to the Director, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research or the Director, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, and the manufacturer must include data derived from nonclinical laboratory and clinical studies that demonstrate safety, purity, and potency. The application must also include financial certification or disclosure statements for clinical investigators. The application shall not be considered filed until all pertinent information and data have been received. A biologics license shall be approved only upon examination of the product and upon a determination that the product complies with the standards established in this chapter. The applicant must also include either a claim for categorical exclusion or an environmental assessment. The license may be reissued or reinstated upon a showing of compliance with requirements. A biologics license shall be issued upon a determination by the Director, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research or the Director, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research that the establishment(s) and the product meet the applicable requirements. A biologics license shall be valid until suspended or revoked. A biologics license shall be revoked upon application of the manufacturer giving notice of intention to discontinue the manufacture of all products manufactured under such license or to discontinue the manufacture of a particular product for which a license is held and waiving an opportunity for a hearing on the matter. A biologics license shall be suspended whenever the Commissioner has reasonable grounds to believe that any of the grounds for revocation of a license exist and that by reason thereof there is a danger to health. A biologics license issued to a manufacturer and covering all locations of manufacture shall authorize persons other than such manufacturer to conduct at places other than such locations the initial, and partial manufacturing of a product for shipment solely to such manufacturer only to the extent that the names of such persons and places are registered with the Commissioner of Food and Drugs and it is found upon application of such manufacturer, that the product is in short supply due either to the peculiar growth requirements of the organism involved or to the scarcity of the animal required for manufacturing purposes, and such manufacturer has established with respect to such persons and places such procedures, inspections, tests, or other arrangements as will ensure full compliance with the applicable regulations of this subchapter related to continued safety, purity, and potency. Such persons and places shall be subject to all regulations of this subchapter except §§ 601.2 to 601.6, 601.9, 601.10, 601.20, 601.21 to 601.33, and 610.60 to 610.65 of this chapter. For persons and places authorized under this section to conduct the initial and partial manufacturing of a product for shipment solely to a manufacturer of a product subject to licensure under § 601.2(c), the following additional regulations shall not be applicable: §§ 600.10(b) and (c), 600.11, 600.12, 600.13, and 610.53 of this chapter.

question: How are manufacturing changes to a licensed biological product reported?
selected_labels: FDA Guidance: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Changes to an Approved Application: Certain Biological Products: Guidance for Industry (final, 2021-06-21, Docket FDA-1995-D-0288)
FDA Guidance: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Changes to an Approved Application: Certain Biological Products: Guidance for Industry (final, 2021-06-21, Docket FDA-1995-D-0288)
answer: The FDA requires that manufacturing changes to a licensed biological product be reported in accordance with the tiered-reporting system, which is based on quality risk assessment and risk management principles. If a change is approved, it must be submitted as a PAS (major change) under 21 CFR 601.12(e). If a change is minor, the CP (change plan) may be submitted for a single or multiple related changes, covering a single or multiple BLAs (biological license applications). The CP may also enable greater predictability in the timing of implementation of CMC changes, placing the product into distribution sooner, and improving the product supply chain planning.
